SMTO-CFG-0055 — A Gateway address in SMTO's startup settings has no name

GUID: a5405e5d-25c8-48f2-aa49-8301f4228122
Slug: config-gateway-endpoint-names-must-be-non-empty
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • One Gateway address in SMTO's startup settings has a blank name. SMTO needs a name to choose that Gateway — the helper program it uses to run commands on a computer — so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who set up SMTO's startup settings which Gateway addresses they added, and find the entry whose name is blank. The startup settings, not the app's Settings page, hold the entry SMTO rejected.
  2. Give that entry a short name, such as the computer's name, or remove the entry if that computer isn't needed. SMTO picks where to run commands by name, so a blank name can't be chosen.
  3. Start SMTO again. To add computers from the app instead, use Settings › Setup › Gateways once SMTO is running. Gateways added on that Settings page are stored separately and don't need a startup entry.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't give the entry the name of a different computer's Gateway; commands meant for one computer could go to the other.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected the gateway_endpoints mapping because one entry's node name is empty after trimming whitespace.

What this means

  • Gateway endpoint normalization produces an empty node name from a configured mapping key. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway endpoint normalization produces an empty node name from a configured mapping key.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect endpoint mapping keys after whitespace normalization; connection health is not checked here.

How to fix it

  • Find the gateway_endpoints mapping passed directly to Settings (Settings(...) or model_validate in embedding code or tests) and rename or remove any key that is empty after trimming, then restart. get_settings does not populate gateway_endpoints, and a bad managed override (managed.json, AOR_MANAGED_SETTINGS_PATH) is reported instead as the generic 'Configuration does not satisfy the settings schema' 422. Gateways registered through Settings > Setup > Gateways are stored separately and need no entry here; this check validates names only, not connectivity.
  • Give each intended Gateway endpoint a nonempty node name.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every configured Gateway endpoint has a nonempty intended node name.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
